Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:192923
Court No. - 66

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 43010 of 2024
Applicant :- Monu @ Mohan Singh

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Vishvendra Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Heard Sri Vishvendra Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
2.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
24 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B, 323 IPC & Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Pinahat,
District Agra, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture, he has been made accused in the present matter.
4. He further submitted that actually deceased pressurized the applicant to live separately in the city but applicant did not want to live in the city after leaving his village and only due to this reason some altercation took place between husband and wife and thereafter, she consumed some poisonous substance and committed suicide.
Monu @ Mohan Singh vs State Of U.P. on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168164381/
1 5.

sentences.text: He further submitted that during post mortem of the deceased, cause of death could not be ascertained and viscera was preserved and viscera report is now on record which suggests that due to consumption of Aluminum Phosphoide, deceased died and therefore, it appears to be a case of suicidal death.

6. He further submitted that during trial, parents of the deceased were examined by the trial court as PW-1 and PW-2 but they did not support the prosecution case and both have been declared hostile and their statements have been annexed alongwith the instant bail application.
7. He further submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 26.2.2024 i.e. for last more than 9 months.

8. Per contra, learned AGA, however, opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within three years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but could not dispute the fact that during trial, parents of the deceased were examined by the trial court as PW-1 and PW-2 but they did not support the prosecution case and both have been declared hostile.

9. He further could not dispute the fact that as per post mortem report, deceased died due to consumption of aluminum phosphide and therefore, possibility of suicide committed by the deceased at this stage cannot be ruled out.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. However, applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within three years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry and torture but it appears that when during trial, parents of the deceased were examined by the trial court as PW-1 and PW-2 then they did not support the prosecution case and both have been declared hostile.

12. Further, during post mortem of the deceased, cause of death could not be ascertained and viscera was preserved and viscera report is now on record which is annexed to the instant bail application and from its perusal it appears that deceased died due to consumption of Aluminum Phosphoide and therefore, considering the viscera report of the deceased, possibility of suicide cannot be ruled out at this stage.
13. Further, applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 26.2.2024 i.e. last more than 9 months.

14. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
15. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

sentences.text:
Let the applicant- Monu @ Mohan Singh, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
17. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

18. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
